description: One loud candle whose trade count rose with its volume, printed while the order book stood at well under half its seven-day median. The book half fails, so the candle is tagged suspect with a completed check.
labelling_rationale: §6.4's second test is the order book: 'order-book depth not anomalously thin (depth >= 50% of its 7-day median)'. SLS v1.0.20 fixes the input: the latest daily depth snapshot taken at or before the candle's close, and the median of the seven snapshots ending at that one. **2026-08-21T00:00 -- the candle.** Volume 500 against the filler's rolling 20-candle H4 median of 100 is RVOL 5.0, the inclusive floor of §6.1's ABNORMAL band, so §6.4 runs. It printed on 30 trades against a 20-candle median of 10 -- exactly 3x, which passes the participants test. **The book.** The candle closes at 2026-08-21T04:00. A daily snapshot carries the start of its UTC day as its stamp but is read later that day, so (owner ruling, Bundle D M2 Q1) a snapshot stamped day D is readable only from D+1 00:00: the newest this candle may read is the one stamped 2026-08-20. The seven ending there are 2026-08-14 .. 2026-08-20: six at 100 and the 2026-08-20 one at 40. Their median is 100, half of it is 50, and 40 is below it, so the depth test fails. **The verdict.** Failing either half tags suspect_volume, so VOLUME_SUSPECT is recorded with rvol 5, participants_ok true, depth_ok false -- and validated true, because both tests ran: this is a completed check that failed, not an incomplete one. **Why nothing else fires.** The candle is a doji under §6.2's 250,000 absolute quote floor (50,000), the same construction as s7-abnormal-volume-cross-validation, which keeps the case to §6.4 alone.
labelled_by: drafted by Claude Opus 5.5 2026-11-23 from SLS §6.4 (v1.0.20); pending developer verification
